A compact neural network designed for un: A compact neural network designed for underwater image enhancement with fewer learned parameters than larger networks. The researchers evaluated it on both synthetic and real underwater images.
improving the appearance of degraded und: improving the appearance of degraded underwater imagery. In ClearWater, try it as an alternative colour treatment for blue/green underwater scenes; compare subjects and neutral tones rather than assuming a more vivid result is more accurate.

Fast Underwater Image Enhancement for Im: Fast Underwater Image Enhancement for Improved Visual Perception. This generative model was designed to improve underwater colour, contrast and visual content, including imagery used for underwater robotic vision.
a fast learned enhancement of underwater: a fast learned enhancement of underwater imagery. Treat it as another look to compare, not a guaranteed improvement: it can introduce an unwanted colour cast, especially on images unlike its training examples. The research's speed results do not predict this app's speed on your phone.

ClearWater uses the authors' PyTorch sam: ClearWater uses the authors' PyTorch sample checkpoint converted to ONNX, rather than the TensorFlow/Keras checkpoint used to reproduce the paper. Paper benchmark results are not claimed for this app.
The model sees a 256 × 256 version of th: The model sees a 256 × 256 version of the original. ClearWater transfers its colour changes onto the image at your chosen export resolution, then applies strength and your manual settings. Full resolution keeps source dimensions and detail, but does not perform full-resolution neural dehazing, denoising or super-resolution. A smaller model download does not necessarily mean faster inference.
ONNX is a portable model-file format. Su: ONNX is a portable model-file format. Supply your own compatible file and choose its documented input and output ranges independently: 0…1 or −1…1. The loader supports self-contained RGB image-to-image models up to 64 MB, with one float32 NCHW input and output compatible with 256 × 256. Models with different layouts, colour orders or extra files need an adapter.
The model is kept in memory and must be: The model is kept in memory and must be loaded again after a reload. Its licence and attribution remain the responsibility of its author and user; loading a file does not grant permission to use or redistribute it. Additional research models are not bundled.

Rebuilds the suggestion using the select: Rebuilds the suggestion using the selected engine and current image or video preview frame, sets strength to 80% and resets manual adjustments. With an AI engine, it does not switch to Balanced. In fixed AI video mode, it also uses the current frame as the reference.
Blends the engine's correction with the: Blends the engine's correction with the original. At 0%, the engine contributes no correction; manual adjustments can still change the image.
Auto uses image analysis without forcing: Auto uses image analysis without forcing Surface or Diving; Diving allows underwater warmth and haze treatment; Surface keeps naturally warm light more conservatively.
Yes tells Balanced to rebalance a filter: Yes tells Balanced to rebalance a filter cast instead of assuming more red is needed. Auto looks for a red/magenta imbalance; No disables that filter assumption.
Blue or Green nudges Balanced's underwat: Blue or Green nudges Balanced's underwater channel balance. Auto estimates it from the image.
A rough hint for Balanced's missing-red: A rough hint for Balanced's missing-red estimate, not the distance from the camera to your subject. Not sure removes the hint. Dive conditions affect Balanced only, not AI models or the original RGB heuristic.
Shifts the balance between warmer reds a: Shifts the balance between warmer reds and cooler blues.
Adjusts a green cast toward magenta, or: Adjusts a green cast toward magenta, or shifts back toward green.
Adds or reduces red independently. Negat: Adds or reduces red independently. Negative settings can help with strong red-filter casts near the surface.
Boosts or reduces colour intensity, with: Boosts or reduces colour intensity, with more emphasis on less saturated colours.
Tap an area that should be neutral white: Tap an area that should be neutral white or grey to rebalance colour. Choose a midtone, avoiding coloured objects, deep shadows and clipped highlights. The choice is cumulative; use Undo if it looks wrong.
Changes overall brightness in stops (EV): Changes overall brightness in stops (EV): +1 roughly doubles the light level; −1 halves it.

Changes separation between lighter and d: Changes separation between lighter and darker tones.
Applies a bounded, global veil/contrast: Applies a bounded, global veil/contrast adjustment. It can improve a washed-out look, but is not a depth-based reconstruction or a way to remove all suspended particles.

Inspect details, return to the fitted vi: Inspect details, return to the fitted view, or hide most of the interface for more image space. Expanded mode keeps adjustments accessible.

MP4 and MOV are containers; the video co: MP4 and MOV are containers; the video codec inside determines whether your device can decode a clip. SDR H.264 is the most predictable starting point. HEVC support depends on the browser/device. HDR and Dolby Vision currently need an SDR copy with proper tone mapping before import.

Strongly different sampled scenes use a matching scene's correction instead of a blend. Short scene changes between samples can be missed.
Shorter intervals follow changes more cl: Shorter intervals follow changes more closely and require more model runs. Five seconds is the default; ten seconds reduces analysis time. Completed samples are reused for manual edits and repeated exports of the active clip.
Estimates one AI colour adjustment from: Estimates one AI colour adjustment from the chosen frame and uses it throughout. Use current frame changes the reference. This reduces analysis when the scene and lighting stay similar.

AI video transfers global colour, not mo: AI video transfers global colour, not moving spatial detail, local dehazing or denoising. Export first analyses any remaining samples, then processes every output frame. Keep the app open; Cancel export stops processing. Input limits: 10 minutes, 512 MB and about 34 megapixels per frame. Output: H.264 MP4, up to 1080p and 30 fps, maximum 256 MB. Longer clips use a lower bitrate. Rotation is baked into exported pixels.
Import JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, compatible: Import JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF, compatible DNG RAW, MP4 or MOV, including multiple files. Android also accepts supported files shared from other apps. Photos up to 60 MB and 45 megapixels proceed normally. Larger photos are allowed with a compact resource notice and resolution options. The safety ceilings are 512 MB per file, 200 megapixels and 32,768 pixels per side; these are not a guarantee that your device can process that much.
Compatible Android DNG and Apple ProRAW: Compatible Android DNG and Apple ProRAW files are developed locally with LibRaw using the camera’s recorded white balance and an sRGB rendering. That becomes an 8-bit image for the existing restoration controls and JPEG/PNG export. This is real RAW development rather than embedded-preview extraction, but it is not a high-bit-depth RAW editor and may look different from the phone’s Photos app. Some compression variants, including JPEG-XL DNG, are unsupported by this decoder. If a DNG cannot be developed, convert it to a compatible DNG, JPEG or HEIC first.
The notice appears only above 45 MP or 6: The notice appears only above 45 MP or 60 MB, or after a processing failure. Larger photos use a small editing preview, with the export-sized image decoded when you save. Auto keeps normal photos full size; for larger photos it uses a conservative target based on available device hints (up to 24 MP on phones/low-memory devices, 45 MP when memory is unknown, or 80 MP on a desktop reporting at least 8 GB). Full resolution explicitly attempts the original dimensions. Reduced caps output at 12 MP. RAW reduction halves each dimension before any further resizing, so 48 MP can become 12 MP. The notice shows the planned export dimensions. Browser memory hints are approximate; some decoders still need full sensor buffers. If processing fails, Retry reduced retains your original and edits. Resolution choices last for the session and do not change your original file.
With an output folder selected, exports: With an output folder selected, exports keep the original stem. Without one, the app uses the source folder where permitted and adds -restore. Browser file pickers do not reveal parent folders, so you may need to choose the source folder once.

JPEG gives smaller photo files with some: JPEG gives smaller photo files with some compression. PNG is lossless and preserves transparency. Both export at the selected photo resolution; Full attempts the original dimensions.
Enabled by default for photo exports. At: Enabled by default for photo exports. Attempts to carry supported EXIF fields from JPEG, PNG, HEIC/HEIF and DNG into the exported JPEG or PNG, including capture dates, camera/lens settings, author/copyright and GPS location when present. Turn it off for an export without source metadata. Rotation is baked into the pixels, so orientation is reset and dimensions and colour-space tags are updated. Old thumbnails, proprietary MakerNotes, XMP/IPTC, source colour profiles and unsupported tags are not copied. PNG metadata support varies between viewers. The app cannot recover metadata already removed by a gallery, sharing app or browser; this depends on the import path, not just the platform. An unreadable metadata block does not stop the photo export; a message reports the failure. Video metadata is not preserved.
A small JSON file containing correction: A small JSON file containing correction settings, not image pixels. It can apply settings to another file. A custom-model recipe records its identity and ranges, but does not include the model itself.

Processing is local; photos, videos and: Processing is local; photos, videos and custom model files are not sent to an inference service. The web app downloads its own assets and supplied model files when needed. Browser storage holds the library and edit recipes, but can be evicted or fill up: retain your originals and export results you want to keep. Supplied web models become available offline after their first successful use; the Android APK includes them.
